title: A hunter and its prey
hook: Compare the effects on both participants.

knows: Ecological interactions can affect participants differently.
doesNotKnow: The predator gains food and the individual prey is harmed, a predation interaction. Population-level effects can be more complex.

misconception: An interaction must affect both participants in the same way.
objective: Classify the stated effects of an ecological interaction.

claims.text: Question, diagram and reveal: A wolf eats a deer, gaining food while the individual deer is killed. Using + for benefit, − for harm and 0 for no appreciable effect, which signs describe Wolf and Deer, in that order? Wolf: +; Deer: −. The predator gains food and the individual prey is harmed, a predation interaction. Population-level effects can be more complex.
claims.source: Stipulated simplified example; ecological definitions: OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-6-community-ecology

claims.text: Icons and signs summarize the stipulated interaction and do not quantify fitness or capture every ecological effect.

Recall: What term describes the Wolf–Deer interaction as stated in the lesson? The predator gains food and the individual prey is harmed, a predation interaction. Population-level effects can be more complex.
